free_tier.stated: per billing account, monthly: 2 million requests, 180,000 vCPU-seconds and 360,000 GiB-seconds under request-based billing; 240,000 vCPU-seconds and 450,000 GiB-seconds under instance-based billing; plus 1 GiB of outbound transfer from North America

per_object_cap.stated: a request may run up to 60 minutes; memory and CPU per instance are configurable

retention.stated: no persistent disk; a container is stateless unless it mounts a volume or a bucket

egress.terms: 1 GiB of data transfer within North America free per month, then Google Cloud network pricing at the Premium tier

interface_detail: an OCI image behind an HTTPS endpoint; the service listens on a port
tooling: gcloud, the Cloud Run API, Docker; any language with an HTTP server
chaining: the only free serverless tier here with 50 vCPU-hours and a listening socket

limits.value: 240,000 vCPU-seconds and 450,000 GiB-seconds a month under instance-based billing
2 million requests a month under request-based billing
1 GiB a month of outbound transfer from North America
an idle instance is billed at the idle rate when a minimum instance is configured; scale to zero is the default

identity_cost.detail: a card at signup; the free tier is a spending-based discount applied after the fact, not a prepaid allowance

reliability_note: a service scales to zero by default and pays a cold start on the next request; a minimum instance removes the cold start and starts the idle meter
confidence_note: both free-tier tables and the per-second rates were read on the pricing page

evidence.proved: Cloud Run free tier: 2 million requests, 360,000 GB-seconds of memory, 180,000 vCPU-seconds, 1 GB of outbound transfer a month
quoted: 'Free tier (based on us-central1 pricing): CPU - First 240,000 vCPU-seconds free per month; RAM - First 450,000 GiB-seconds free per month' under instance-based billing
quoted: 'CPU - First 180,000 vCPU-seconds free per month; RAM - First 360,000 GiB-seconds free per month; Requests - 2 million requests free per month' under request-based billing
quoted: 'The free tier usage is aggregated across projects by billing account and resets every month'
quoted rate table: 'CPU (per vCPU-second) ... $0.000018', 'Memory (per GiB-second) ... $0.000002', 'Idle time (Min instance1) $0.0000025'

notes: Arithmetic from the published free tiers, not a measurement: at 0.25 vCPU and 512 MiB, an always-on instance needs 648,000 vCPU-seconds and 1,296,000 GiB-seconds a month. The memory grant runs out first, at 900,000 seconds, so the free tier holds an always-on 0.25 vCPU service for about 10.4 days a month. What is not verified is whether the 'Idle time (Min instance)' SKU is drawn from the same free tier; the page presents it as a separate rate.

keep_rate.basis: a scaled-to-zero service does not bill

session_cap.note: a request may run 60 minutes; the service scales to zero when idle unless a minimum instance is set

network_out.ports: the container port on a generated HTTPS hostname

extras.open_question: whether the grant applies to the Services meter or the Instances meter
extras.gap: the grant's meter (Services or Instances) is not resolved; the claim page's Instances section and footnotes would close it
extras.price_arithmetic: free within the monthly grant; 512 MiB at 0.25 vCPU consumes the 450,000 GiB-second grant in 900,000 s = 10.4 days of 24/7

binding_note: an always-on instance spends the monthly grant in about ten days: 450,000 GiB-seconds at 512 MiB is 900,000 seconds, 10.4 days.
tier: Free tier, request-based and instance-based billing
